source_evidence: Registered index-linked annuities (RILAs) increase or decrease contract value during the accumulation phase, based, in part, on the performance of a specified benchmark
answer: A registered index-linked annuity (RILA) is a deferred annuity whose contract value can rise or fall during the accumulation phase partly in response to a specified benchmark, such as a stock index. The insurer credits interest at the end of a specified term, and you do not know the interest rate in advance. Unlike a fixed indexed annuity, a RILA can lose money when index performance is poor. Insurers generally set limits on both potential gains and losses, though the details vary by contract.
